key_insight: HemAutomaton enables whole-slide white blood cell extraction and profiling without manual region selection, expanding automated analysis to tens of thousands of cells per smear.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support more comprehensive blood cancer assessments through automated differential and blast counting, rather than drug discovery.
method: Neural cellular automata detect white blood cells across entire blood and bone marrow smear images.
A pretrained hematology foundation model enables few-shot cell classification with limited annotations.
Slide-wide spatial analysis maps variation in blast frequency.
evidence_signal: Across three blood cancer cohorts, researchers extracted over 100 million cell images; detection matched Faster R-CNN in-domain and surpassed it under domain shifts, while automated blast counts agreed with experts within inter-expert variability.
watch_item: Prospective validation across independent laboratories and scanning workflows is needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Exhaustive white blood cell extraction and profiling across whole-slide images of blood and bone marrow smears
